items.summary: Board President Rafael Mandelman called the regular meeting of October 7, 2025, to order and the clerk conducted roll call. The Board recited the ancestral homeland acknowledgment and the Pledge of Allegiance, and acknowledged the staff of SFGovTV.

The Clerk of the Board announced instructions for public participation, including in-person attendance in the legislative chamber, viewing options on SFGovTV, submitting written comment, and requesting accommodations.

The Board considered the approval of the meeting minutes from the September 2, 2025 regular board meeting. On a motion by Supervisor Melgar, seconded by Supervisor Dorsey, the minutes were approved unanimously.
The Board considered the consent agenda consisting of Items 1 through 4. With no supervisor requesting any item be removed, the consent agenda passed unanimously.

The Board considered Items 1 through 4 on the consent agenda, covering contracting requirements, public works graffiti abatement, landmark designation of Mint Mall at 951-957 Mission Street, and the Neighborhood Beautification and Graffiti Clean-up Fund. The ordinances were finally passed on a unanimous roll call vote.

The Board considered a resolution authorizing the Recreation and Parks Department to accept and expend an in-kind grant valued at approximately $580,000 from the Dogpatch and Northwest Potrero Hill Green Benefit District for the design and construction of the 22nd Street pathway steps. The resolution was adopted without objection.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively approving a grant agreement between the City and the San Francisco Unified School District for the Student Success Fund for up to $28,996,871 from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026. The resolution was adopted without objection.

The Board approved a lease amendment with MRG San Francisco Terminal 2, LLC for concession retail space at San Francisco International Airport, adding three locations across a 12-year term with no adjustment to the minimum annual guarantee. The resolution was adopted without objection.

The Board approved a second amendment to the contract with AT&T Mobility for public safety-grade wireless communications services for first responders. The amendment extended the term through April 21, 2027, and increased the contract amount by approximately $7.3 million for a new total not to exceed $29,572,719.

The Board considered a contract with Golden Gate Petroleum to supply diesel fuel for city operations for up to $195,000,000 over five years, with options to extend. The resolution was called together with Item 10 and adopted without objection.

The Board considered a contract with Pacific Coast Petroleum for gasoline fuel supply for up to $93,000,000 over an initial five-year term with extension options. The resolution was adopted without objection.

The Board considered a grant agreement amendment between the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing and the San Francisco Health Plan under the Housing and Homelessness Incentive Program. The amendment adds $2.82 million for a total not to exceed $6,047,884 to fund enhanced onsite services and data integration in permanent supportive housing.

The Board approved a resolution retroactively authorizing the District Attorney's Office to accept and expend a $233,256 grant from the California Department of Industrial Relations to implement a wage theft enforcement program through July 31, 2026.

The Board authorized the Department of Public Health to apply for grants in excess of $25 million from the California Department of Health Care Services under the Behavioral Health Infrastructure Bond Act Round 2 Unmet Needs Program. Supervisor Dorsey spoke in co-sponsorship and welcomed students from Civics Lab attending the meeting.

items.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the Building and Planning Codes to comply with state law (SB 937) by postponing the collection of development impact fees on residential projects until the issuance of the first certificate of occupancy. After clarifying questions from Supervisor Walton to the Department of Building Inspection and the City Attorney, the ordinance passed on first reading 10-1, with Supervisor Fielder dissenting.

speakers.name: Rafael Mandelman

items.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the General Plan Urban Design Element and Downtown Area Plan to facilitate the 530 Sansome mixed-use tower and Fire Station 13 development project. Heard in conjunction with related project items, the ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

The Board considered an ordinance amending the Planning Code and Zoning Map to establish the 530 Sansome Mixed-Use Tower and Fire Station Special Use District, conditionally rescinding the landmark designation for 447 Battery Street, and raising height limits. The ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

The Board considered an ordinance approving a major encroachment permit for portions of Merchant Street adjacent to the 530 Sansome project for roadway and sidewalk paving, crosswalks, overhead lighting, and streetscape improvements. The ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

The Board approved an amended and restated conditional property exchange agreement with EQX Jackson SQ Holdco LLC for the exchange of 530 Sansome Street and 447 Battery Street to construct a new Fire Station 13. The ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

The Board considered a development agreement with EQX Jackson SQ Holdco LLC for the 530 Sansome and Fire Station 13 project, securing approximately $4.3 million in additional affordable housing payments and establishing community benefits. The ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

The Board approved a hotel and fire station development incentive agreement providing up to $86 million net present value over 25 years in financial assistance from transient occupancy taxes for the 530 Sansome project. The ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

The Board considered an ordinance amending the Building Code to allow affordable housing projects and certain other projects to defer payment of certain administrative fees. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

The Board considered a resolution urging the Controller's City Services Auditor and the Department of Public Works to develop objective streetscape, stairway, and landscape maintenance standards to support small businesses and commercial corridors. The resolution was adopted without objection.

The Board adopted a resolution accepting the African American Arts and Cultural District's Cultural, History, Housing, and Economic Sustainability Strategy Report pursuant to Administrative Code Section 107.5.

The Board approved an ordinance on first reading amending the Administrative Code to add Protecting San Francisco, a nonprofit supporting San Francisco Deputy Sheriffs and their families, to the list of organizations eligible for employee payroll deduction donations.
The Board approved a motion appointing Sascha Bittner and Nicole Bohn to the In-Home Supportive Services Public Authority for terms ending March 1, 2027.

The Board held its special order recognizing commendations for meritorious service. Commendations were presented to Sing Tao Daily publisher Joseph Leung, the San Francisco Bar Pilots on their 175th anniversary, Paul Giusti of the Italian-American Social Club, and Eva Chuang and the Department of Public Works Bureau of Urban Forestry team.

items.summary: The Board convened its 3:00 p.m. special order for a Committee of the Whole hearing on implementation of US Department of Justice recommendations for police reform. On a motion by Supervisor Walton, seconded by Supervisor Fielder, the hearing was continued to November 18, 2025.

items.summary: The Board convened a Committee of the Whole hearing on findings and recommendations regarding law enforcement practices and US DOJ reforms. Supervisor Walton moved to continue the hearing to allow the Police Department's new administration time to prepare, which was approved without objection to November 18, 2025.

Supervisors introduced new business and in memoriams during Roll Call for Introductions. Introductions included legislation extending the Fisherman's Wharf Ferris wheel, design standards hearings, affordable housing funding inquiries, a mandate for drug-free permanent supportive housing, and resolutions honoring Joey Alexander, United Against Hate Week, and Pregnancy and Infant Loss Remembrance Day.

items.summary: The Board heard general public comment from community members. Speakers addressed concerns regarding surveillance technologies and cyberstalking, parcel tax policies impacting homeowners, tech architecture and project funding, and child protection advocacy.

The Board considered Items 30 through 38 on the Adoption Without Committee Reference calendar, covering immigrant healthcare rights, Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts, clinical social worker compensation at UCSF, election results declaration, and municipal code updates. The resolutions were adopted on a 10-0 roll call vote, with Supervisor Walton absent, and the meeting adjourned in memory of Joe Betz, Diana Moon-Wong Liao-Landers, and Joey Alexander.
